name: 24LC08BT-I_SN
title: 24AA08 / 24LC08B: 8 Kbit (1024 x 8) I2C serial EEPROM
summary: An 8 Kbit electrically erasable PROM arranged as four blocks of 256 bytes, reached over a two-wire I2C-compatible bus at up to 400 kHz. The 24AA08 runs from 1.7 V to 5.5 V (100 kHz below 2.5 V) and the 24LC08B from 2.5 V to 5.5 V. Writes go through a 16-byte page buffer and complete in a self-timed cycle of 5 ms maximum; a WP pin locks the whole array against writes. The address pins A0 to A2 have no internal connection. 24LC08BT-I/SN is the 24LC08B, industrial range, 8-lead SOIC, on tape and reel.
key_figures: 3 mA at VCC = 5.5 V, SCL = 400 kHz
5 ms max (byte or page); page write 3 ms typ

notes: An order code is device, then '-', then the temperature letter, then '/', then the package code. Devices: 24AA08, 24AA08T, 24LC08B, 24LC08BT; a T after the device name means tape and reel.
Temperature: I = -40 °C to +85 °C, E = -40 °C to +125 °C. The 24AA08 comes in the I range only.

Package codes: P = 8-lead plastic DIP, 300 mil body; SN = 8-lead plastic SOIC, 3.90 mm body; ST = 8-lead plastic TSSOP, 4.4 mm; MC = 8-lead 2x3 DFN; MS = 8-lead plastic MSOP; OT = 5-lead SOT-23, tape and reel only; MNY = 8-lead TDFN, 2x3 mm body, with NiPdAu finish (the Y).

Packages are lead (Pb) free and RoHS compliant. Factory programming is offered.

operation.text: 1024 bytes in four blocks of 256. Block-select bits B1 and B0 in the control byte pick the block and act as the top two bits of the 10-bit address; the next byte, A7 to A0, picks the byte inside the block.
The memory is always a slave. A master drives SCL, owns the bus and creates the Start and Stop conditions; either side may send or receive, as the master decides.

Idle: SDA and SCL both high, and a transfer begins only then. SDA may change only while SCL is low; a change with SCL high is a condition. Start is SDA falling with SCL high and opens every command; Stop is SDA rising with SCL high and closes every operation. A data bit is valid when SDA holds steady through the high half of its clock; one clock per bit.

The addressed receiver acknowledges each byte by holding SDA low through the high period of a ninth clock that the master supplies, meeting setup and hold times. While an internal write is running the device acknowledges nothing. When reading, the master signals the last byte by leaving it unacknowledged; the memory then releases SDA high so the master can send Stop.
The first byte after Start is the control byte: control code 1010, then B2 (ignored), B1, B0, then R/W (1 read, 0 write). The device watches SDA after every Start and acknowledges when it sees 1010.

Master sends Start, the control byte with R/W = 0, the word address, then one data byte; the device acknowledges each. Stop starts the self-timed internal write, during which the device does not acknowledge.

As a byte write, but the master keeps sending up to 16 data bytes before Stop. They collect in the 16-byte buffer and are programmed together after Stop. Each byte advances only the low four address bits; the upper seven bits stay fixed. Pages begin at multiples of 16. Bytes beyond the end of a page wrap to its start and overwrite what was loaded there, so only the last 16 bytes sent are kept. Software must keep a page write inside one page.
WP at VCC protects the full array, 000 to 3FF, against writes; WP at VSS removes the protection. Reads are unaffected.

Right after the Stop that starts a write, the master can send Start and a write control byte (R/W = 0) repeatedly. No ACK means the write cycle is still running; an ACK means it is done and a further command may follow. It keeps bus throughput high.

An internal address counter holds the last address used plus one. A control byte with R/W = 1 makes the device acknowledge and send the byte at that address; the master does not acknowledge it and sends Stop.

The master first sets the address by starting a write: control byte with R/W = 0 and the word address. After that byte is acknowledged it sends a new Start (no Stop), then the control byte with R/W = 1. The device acknowledges and sends the addressed byte; the master leaves it unacknowledged and sends Stop.

Begun like a random or current-address read, but the master acknowledges each byte it receives, and the device sends the next address in turn. The address pointer advances after every byte, so the entire memory can be read in one operation. The master ends with no ACK and Stop.

A VCC detector disables the internal erase/write circuits when VCC is below 1.5 V at nominal conditions. SCL and SDA have Schmitt-trigger inputs and filters that reject spikes (TSP 50 ns max), and the output edge rate is slope-controlled against ground bounce.

On SCL: TR (4), TF (5), THIGH (2) and TLOW (3). On SDA as an input: TSU:STA (7) and THD:STA (6) at Start, THD:DAT (8) and TSU:DAT (9) around each SCL edge, TSU:STO (10) at Stop, TBUF (12) between a Stop and the next Start, and spike suppression TSP (14). On SDA as an output: TAA (11), from SCL falling to valid data. The SCL input hysteresis is VHYS (D4).
CMOS: read current 1 mA max and standby current 1 µA max. Standby is specified with SDA = SCL = VCC and WP = VSS.
